correctness.rationale: Specializing the published generator equations to four order statistics fixes the generator mean and variance as \(m=(3c+2b)/(3a+4b+3c)\) and \(v=(9ac-4b^2)/(3a+4b+3c)^2\). Boundary equality is exactly \(v=0\), forcing a unique degenerate generator and hence, by the published one-to-one generator/normalized-parent map, a unique two-point parent; direct four-sample gap formulas give the displayed atoms. In the strict interior, \(0<v<m(1-m)\), and the stated open one-parameter family of two-atom generators has exactly mean \(m\) and variance \(v\). The associated explicit three-point parents have the required generator and therefore the required four expected order statistics. The packaged checker also computes their order-statistic expectations directly.

value.rationale: The four-term case is the first nontrivial finite expected-order-statistic feasibility problem in the primary source. The new result turns its quadratic feasible region into a complete identification phase diagram: every boundary point identifies one explicit two-point parent, while every interior point is already nonidentified inside the smallest natural enlargement to three-point parents. This directly answers a structural question about what four expected order statistics determine, rather than adding a routine numerical instance.
